newsitem.title: CHINA: Most Hong Kong people expect no changes - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Hong Kong people expect no changes - poll.

text.p: The majority of people in Hong Kong do not expect great changes under Chinese rule, an opinion poll indicated on Tuesday.
The telephone poll, conducted by Hong Kong University, interviewed 555 people just hours before Britain handed the territory back to China at midnight on Monday.
Almost 61 percent said they did not believe there would be significant changes in Hong Kong after the handover. Only 18 percent expected great changes.
More than 40 percent of respondents believed Hong Kong's international status would become more important, compared with 13 percent saying it would lose its importance.
The survey also found many respondents were neutral.
Almost 48 percent said their feelings were neutral, while 35 percent were happy and only nine percent were apprehensive about China's take over.
